images.what: Page 1 of the Hawaiʻi Department of Health's August 22, 2022 report, "Rapid survey among Hawaiʻi medical cannabis patients and providers on the potential effects of legalization of adult use," with the state seal, the title and the report date.
Page 19 of the same report. The last lines of the page say dispensary workers are the next most relied-upon source, with 56% of patients obtaining information from them.

Page 20 of the report with Figure 10, a bar chart of the sources patients rely on for medical information about cannabis: medical provider 66.2%, dispensary employees 55.9%, health care professional websites and conferences 31.5%, Hawaiʻi Department of Health 15.6%. Number of responses 2217.

Part of page 27 of the report, an appendix page that prints question 14 of the patient questionnaire, "Who do you rely on for medical information about cannabis? (Check all that apply)," with six answer choices.
Page 7 of the report, the Limitations section. It says the surveys used convenience sampling with opt-in participation, so the results do not represent the program's patient and provider populations.
Illustrative photo: the front of a medical marijuana dispensary in Ypsilanti, Michigan. It is not in Hawaii; the study on this slide surveyed staff in other states.

Page 1 of OMCCR's Medical Cannabis Registry Program report with data as of August 31, 2026: 29,315 valid registrations, 2,342 caregivers, and 248 physicians and APRNs who have certified one or more currently registered patients.

First half of section 521-39 in large type, showing that an eviction provision is void unless the rental agreement allows eviction for smoking tobacco and the medical cannabis is used by means of smoking

Later part of section 521-39 in large type, from the end of the smoking exception to the closing proviso that the section does not apply where the proviso that the section does not apply where condominium or planned community documents prohibit the medical use of cannabis

Page 2 of Act 170, Session Laws of Hawaii 2017, showing section 2, which lists the sections whose references to marijuana become cannabis, including 421J-16, 514B-113 and 521-39
